title: The Hiding H
kidRule: H likes to hide! It is quiet at the very start of a few words, like HONEST and HEIR, and it is quiet right after R or G at the start of a word, as in RHYME and GHERKIN.
hint: Careful, a quiet letter is hiding in this word. We do not hear it at all! Which letter is it, and where does it go?
reminder: A quiet H hides in this word: at the very start, or right after the R or G.

check.question: Why can't we hear the H in RHYME?
check.correctAnswer: H is quiet when it comes right after G or R at the start of a word!
distractors: Because poem words never say their second letter
Because the letter Y makes the letter before it quiet

words.sent: An honest person gives back what they find.
words.story: The American president Abraham Lincoln was so truthful that people called him 'Honest Abe'!
words.card: *One* *honest* crow gave back all the shiny spoons!

words.def: A word that ends with the same sound as another word, like cat and hat.
words.sent: Can you think of a rhyme for the word frog?
words.story: It is very hard to find a perfect rhyme for the words orange, silver, and month!
words.card: 'Find a *rhyme* for *me*,' said the bee, 'and I will share my tea!'

words.def: A huge gray animal with thick skin and one or two horns on its nose.
words.sent: The rhino cooled off in a muddy pool.
words.story: A rhino's horn is made of keratin, the very same stuff as your fingernails!
words.card: '*No*, I will not wear a tutu,' said the *rhino*, but he did anyway!

words.def: A shape with four sides that are all the same length, like a diamond.
words.sent: The diamond on a playing card is a rhombus.
words.story: A square is a special kind of rhombus, one that has four square corners!
words.card: The school *bus* was squished into a *rhombus* by a hugging giant!

words.def: A small cucumber that has been pickled in vinegar.
words.sent: I put a crunchy gherkin on my sandwich.
words.story: A tall, rounded glass skyscraper in London is nicknamed 'The Gherkin' because of its pickle shape!
words.card: The *gherkin* said the cucumber was its *kin*, only less sour!

words.def: The person who will get a family's crown, land, or treasures one day.
words.sent: The young princess was heir to the throne.
words.story: In many kingdoms, the heir to the throne is the oldest child of the king or queen!
words.card: *He* is the *heir* to a giant pile of teddy bears!

words.def: Great respect, or something that makes you feel very proud.
words.sent: It was an honor to carry the flag in the parade.
words.story: In Britain this word is spelled with an extra letter U near the end!
words.card: It is an *honor* to sit *on* the royal beanbag chair!

words.sent: He dressed up as a green ghoul for Halloween.
words.story: This word came into English from old Arabic stories about a monster that lived in the desert!
words.card: '*Ho* ho ho,' laughed the *ghoul*, 'I only eat marshmallows!'

words.def: A plant with long pink stems that are cooked into pies.
words.sent: Grandpa baked a rhubarb pie for dessert.
words.story: Only the pink stems of this plant are for eating. Its big green leaves are poisonous!
words.card: The pirate traded a gold *bar* for one slice of *rhubarb* pie!

words.def: A pattern of beats or sounds that repeats, like in music.
words.sent: We clapped our hands to the rhythm of the drum.
words.story: Your heart keeps its own steady beat, about 100,000 times every single day!
words.card: The mo*th* tapped a *rhythm* on the lamp with all six feet!
words.trick: Rhythm Helps Your Two Hips Move: R-H-Y-T-H-M!
